st: Tesla, VanMoof, Duracell? Who will win the sustainable-mobility race?

sec.t: ff.5.1 All that glitters is not green
sec.p: A petrol city car that pollutes less than a Tesla? A promising Dutch start-up, Lightyear One, shows that not all that glitters is gold, or green. In fact, small cars with traditional engines pollute less than a Tesla Model S over their entire life cycle.
Not just cars: with 3 GWh of capacity (25% of the total) Tesla controls a good chunk of the world's electricity storage potential. And they aim to reach 1,500 GWh (500x) by 2030.
During the pandemic, e-bikes outsold electric cars (500k bikes vs 250k cars in the United States).
If e-bikes are the next frontier of mobility, VanMoof is the Tesla of two wheels. Below, the Model V, which will reach 50 km/h and cost €3500:

Have you watched Squid Game? No? If you spend at least 30 minutes a day getting to and from work, you could have watched it 15 times this year alone. Or watched 80 films. On average in the United States (but I don't think Milan is much different), commutes are actually longer…
